vt18_relations_record.topic: Holy See–Israel relations 1994–2026: Legal Personality Agreement, the unfinished economic/fiscal agreement, papal visits, nuncios, frictions and cooperation

claims.text: Legal Personality Agreement signed in Jerusalem on 10 November 1997: Israel gives full effect in Israeli law to the legal personality of the Catholic Church, Eastern Catholic patriarchates, the Latin Patriarchate, dioceses, the Custody of the Holy Land and other entities; legal transactions governed by Israeli law, internal matters by canon law; entities deemed to consent to be sued in Israeli courts; Art. 13: in force on the later notification of ratification.

Wikipedia: Fundamental Agreement in force 10 March 1994; nunciature and Israeli embassy opened 19 January 1994; full relations 15 June 1994; first Israeli ambassador Shmuel Hadas presented credentials 29 September 1994; joint commission met briefly in 1994 and not again until 2004; talks broke down 10 December 2009 (Deputy FM Danny Ayalon spoke of a crisis), resumed 2010; no comprehensive tax and property agreement.

AsiaNews, 1 May 2009: negotiations on the economic agreement began on 11 March 1999; plenary reported 'significant progress' but no agreement before Benedict XVI's visit; issues: recognition of historic tax exemptions, protection of Church property, restitution (e.g. Caesarea church expropriated and razed in the 1950s).

NC Register, 22 June 2012: commission at the Vatican 11–12 June 2012 noted 'significant progress'; Catholic Ordinaries of the Holy Land said 'a signing is not imminent'; the agreement was originally due within two years of 1993; Msgr Ettore Balestrero said talks would not address East Jerusalem or the West Bank.

Holy See Press Office, 14 June 2017: plenary in Vatican City on 13 June 2017 under FA Art. 10(2), heads Msgr Antoine Camilleri and Minister Tzachi Hanegbi, hoped for a 'rapid conclusion of ongoing negotiations'; acknowledged implementation of the 1997 Legal Personality Agreement. No later joint communiqué and no signed economic agreement found in searches to 22 October 2026.

John Paul II at the Western Wall, 26 March 2000: 'we are deeply saddened by the behaviour of those who in the course of history have caused these children of yours to suffer' and 'asking your forgiveness we wish to commit ourselves to genuine brotherhood with the people of the Covenant'.

Benedict XVI at Yad Vashem, 11 May 2009: 'they will never lose their names'; Rabbi Israel Meir Lau said something was missing, noting 'killed' not 'murdered' and no apology; did not visit the museum hall with the Pius XII caption; background of the Williamson excommunication lifting.

Francis, May 2014: prayed at the separation barrier in Bethlehem (25 May), used 'state of Palestine'; first pope to lay a wreath at Herzl's grave; at Netanyahu's request stopped at a memorial to terror victims (26 May); at Yad Vashem: 'Grant us the grace to be ashamed'; invited Peres and Abbas to a Vatican prayer for peace the following month.

Apostolic nuncios to Israel: Montezemolo 1994–1998; Pietro Sambi 1998–2005; Antonio Franco 2006–2012; Giuseppe Lazzarotto 2012–2017; Leopoldo Girelli 2017–2021; Adolfo Tito Yllana 2021–2026; Giorgio Lingua from 22 January 2026; the nunciature is in Jaffa/Tel Aviv; the nuncio is also apostolic delegate in Jerusalem and Palestine.

31 December 2025: Latin Patriarchate said Caritas Jerusalem is an Ecclesiastical Legal Person in Israel recognized under the 1993 Fundamental Agreement and the 1997 Legal Personality Agreement, had not undertaken re-registration with Israeli authorities, and would continue operating in Gaza, the West Bank and Jerusalem.

EFE (2 Sept 2025, from the Israeli presidency): Herzog to meet Leo XIV and Parolin on 4 September 2025 on antisemitism, hostages and Christian communities; Herzog attended Leo's inauguration; only Israel's ambassador attended Francis's funeral; Netanyahu's office took three days to issue condolences.

Good Friday 3 April 2026: Leo XIV phoned President Herzog; Holy See readout: 'the need to reopen all possible channels of diplomatic dialogue was reiterated', protecting civilians and international humanitarian law; Herzog's office said they discussed Iranian missile threats and Christians in Lebanon; context: the US and Israel-led war in Iran, expanded to Lebanon.

Palm Sunday 29 March 2026: Israeli police stopped Cardinal Pizzaballa and Fr Francesco Ielpo (Custos) from reaching the Holy Sepulchre, citing Iran-war security; Latin Patriarchate: prevented 'for the first time in centuries'; Meloni called it an offence; Tajani said he would summon Israel's ambassador; Macron condemned it.

Same day Netanyahu said Pizzaballa had 'full and immediate access'; Herzog said the incident stemmed from security concerns over Iranian missile threats; no Holy See statement reported; Leo paid tribute to Middle East Christians.

vt18_palestine_record.topic: Holy See and Palestine: Basic Agreement with the PLO (15 February 2000), the 2012 UN vote, Comprehensive Agreement (2015/2016), Abbas visits, Leo XIV and the two-state position to 2026

claims.text: Basic Agreement between the Holy See and the PLO signed in the Vatican on 15 February 2000 (Latin note: XV m. Februarii anno MM) by Mgr Celestino Migliore and Dr Emile Jarjoui; preamble calls for 'a special statute for Jerusalem, internationally guaranteed' and declares 'unilateral decisions and actions altering the specific character and status of Jerusalem' morally and legally unacceptable; Art. 4 Status Quo; Art. 12 in force on signature. No reference to 15 January.

Holy See welcomed 'with favour' the UNGA decision of 29 November 2012 making Palestine a non-member observer state; called for an internationally guaranteed special statute for Jerusalem; quoted Benedict XVI: two-state solution should 'become a reality, not remain a dream'; cites the Basic Agreement of 15 February 2000.

26 June 2015 at the Apostolic Palace: Archbishop Paul Gallagher and Foreign Minister Riad al-Malki signed the Comprehensive Agreement (preamble, 32 articles, 8 chapters); Gallagher linked the State of Palestine as signatory to the UNGA resolution of 29 November 2012 and hoped for 'the much desired two-State solution'; al-Malki said it included the Holy See's official recognition of Palestine as a state; the bulletin dates the Basic Agreement 15 February 2000.
2 January 2016: Holy See announced the agreement 'has come into full force' after notifications under Art. 30; it 'regards essential aspects of the life and activity of the Church in Palestine'.

14 January 2017: Abbas met Francis for about 23 minutes, then Parolin and Gallagher, and inaugurated the Palestinian embassy to the Holy See; he called it a 'sign that the Pope loves the Palestinian people'. (CNA dates the Comprehensive Agreement's signing 13 May 2015, which is wrong: the text was concluded then and signed 26 June 2015.)

6 November 2025: Leo XIV received Abbas, marking the 10th anniversary of the Comprehensive Agreement; both noted the 'urgent need to provide assistance to the civilian population in Gaza' and discussed a two-State solution.

30 November 2025, flight Istanbul–Beirut, Leo XIV: 'We all know that at present, Israel still does not accept this solution'; 'We are also friends with Israel, and we are trying to act as a mediating voice for both parties.'

Vatican News 17 August 2026: Leo XIV told the diplomatic corps on 9 January 2026 that the two-state solution 'remains the institutional perspective'; Benedict XVI in 2009 supported 'a sovereign Palestinian homeland'; Francis in 2014 called for 'the acknowledgment by all of the right of two States to exist'.

Parolin at the UN General Assembly, September 2026: two-state solution 'the only viable and equitable path'; Holy See 'continues to uphold the inalienable rights of the Palestinian people'; repeated call for an internationally guaranteed special statute for Jerusalem; welcomed the 2025 Gaza resolution as a positive step but said Gaza cannot be separated from the Palestinian future as a whole.
